title: Letter 6 — On Christian Wisdom
attribution_note: Letter 6 of 46 in the collection Letters Sent — see Letter 1 for provenance.

sections.heading: To know God, and walk before Him

pairs.en: Here, too, as far as I am able, I write to you also of Christian wisdom, about which you once asked me, and which we must learn all our life long. Consider, then, the following:

1) To know the one true God, to fear Him and love Him above all things and above one's own self; to show Him obedience, submission and heartfelt compliance; to thank Him from the heart for all the kindnesses shown and still being shown to us — that He created us, that He so wondrously redeemed us in our fallenness, that He feeds, clothes and keeps us, and furnishes us with the other goods of this world; to call upon Him from the heart, to ask and expect from Him help, intercession and mercy; to hope in Him with all one's heart; in a word, to honour Him as His holy word teaches us — in this consists Christian wisdom.

2) God is in every place, and there is no place where God is not. Therefore, whatever we do, say and think, we do, say and think before His holy eyes: whatever a man says, He hears; whatever he does and thinks, He sees, and writes it in His book, and on the last day will render to every man according to his deeds, plans, words and undertakings. Nothing is hidden from Him — not only what is done in a secret place, but what is devised and done in the heart. This His Holy Scripture teaches us, and our faith, which has His Holy Scripture for its foundation. For upon the foundation of Holy Scripture our faith and all our piety are established. Therefore every Christian must act, in all his deeds, words, thoughts and dealings with his neighbour, with fear — just as subjects act and walk in the presence of their king, and servants before their master, and children before their father. Before an earthly king we dare not, and are ashamed to, do anything contrary; much more must nothing be done that is contrary to God. Blessed and wise is he who so lives and walks before God, and pleases Him!

3) To guard oneself in every way against every sin in word, deed and thought, since every sin is committed before the God who is everywhere present and sees all, and every sin offends the great God, and deprives the sinner of His mercy, and exposes him to His righteous wrath. [Romans 1:18] Blessed and wise is he who avoids this deadly poison, which puts to death forever both the soul and body of man.

4) To think and hold that the great God speaks, commands and promises in His Holy Scripture to me and to you, just as to all men. For God is no respecter of persons, but *“will have all”* equally *“to be saved, and to come unto the knowledge of the truth”* [1 Timothy 2:4]; therefore He speaks to all in the Scripture that has been given to us by Him for our salvation. From this will follow faith in His holy and merciful promises, and diligent performance of His holy commandments. For if an earthly king makes a promise, we believe him and expect it from him, and whatever he commands us, we carry out with diligence; how much more shall we believe God, and without doubt expect and hope from Him what He promises us, and strive to carry out what He commands us, once we are exactly assured that it is He who commands and promises us.

God alone must be believed above the whole world, and His holy word carried out above every human word, since every man, however great, and the whole world besides, is as nothing before God. Whoever loves and honours God, loves and honours His word as a great thing too. A king's word and letter is honoured as a great thing; much more must the Word of God, sent to us from Him, as a letter, through the prophets and apostles, be honoured as a great and precious thing.

sections.heading: A stranger passing through a dream

pairs.en: 5) A man living in this world is a stranger, a pilgrim, and a wayfarer. He enters the world, and after living a little while, departs from it, like one who, having sojourned in a foreign land, returns again to his fatherland and his home. So a man too lives for a while in the world and departs from the world. Life in this world, and everything in it — honour, glory, riches, luxury and the rest — is like a dream, for all this appears for a short while and soon passes away, like a dream. For death, when it comes, takes away life, and with life, everything a man has. As all are born equal, so all die equal — except that one departs righteous and another sinful, one blessed and another wretched and poor. Death makes all men equal: the rich man is stripped of his riches, the glorious of his glory, the honoured of his honour, and the luxurious of his luxury. The graves of the dead show this. Where the master lies, where his servant lies, where the glorious, where the inglorious, where the rich, where the poor — it is impossible to tell. Here all are made equal, all have returned to the earth as earth, and over them walk not only every sort of man, but the cattle too.

Consider here what man is, and his life, and his thought. Man is *“earth and ashes”*; *“verily, every man living is altogether vanity.* *Surely man walketh in a vain shadow, he disquieteth himself in vain, he heapeth up riches, and knoweth not who shall gather them.”* [Sirach 10:9; Psalm 38:6–7] And *“they leave their riches to strangers, and their graves are their houses for ever, their dwelling-places to all generations.”* [Psalm 48:11–12] Wise is he who understands this. Blessed is he who lives in this world as a wayfarer, a pilgrim and a stranger, and always lifts the eyes of his soul toward his heavenly fatherland.

6) Since everything in the world, like a dream, departs from us at death, and we dwell in this world as strangers, pilgrims and wayfarers, entering upon this road at our birth and ending it at our death, wisdom and blessedness consist in this: to cling to nothing in this world, but to regard everything — honour, glory, riches, and all this world's treasure — as a dream, which comes to us with sleep and departs with sleep; and to cling to God alone, the highest good and the source of all good, and to seek and love the eternal treasure, so that where our treasure is, there our heart may be also; *“to set our mind on things above, and not on things on the earth.”* [Colossians 3:2] In this consists Christian wisdom.

sections.heading: Riches, office, and the four last things

pairs.en: 7) If riches are given to anyone by God, let him not spend them on luxury and excessive buildings, but be content with them in moderation, and thank God, and provide for the poor, the needy and the destitute, to the glory of God. If an honourable position is given to anyone, let him, while holding it, care for the glory of God and the good of society, and not serve mammon. If glory and praise are given to anyone, let him count himself unworthy of it, but ascribe it all to God alone. For to Him alone belongs all glory and praise, as the Source of all good things, while it befits man, as a sinner, to be humble. *“Not unto us, O Lord, not unto us, but unto Thy name give glory.”* [Psalm 113:9] Wise and blessed is he who acts thus.

8) Always to have before the eyes of the soul, or to keep in remembrance, death, the universal judgment of Christ, eternal torment and the heavenly kingdom. Just as every man must certainly die, though when, how and where is unknown, so must all men certainly appear before Christ's judgment, and give account to the righteous Judge for their words, deeds and thoughts. And as the righteous will have life with all the treasure of heaven, so the unrepentant sinners will have eternal torment in fire and in Tartarus. So God, true and without falsehood, has declared in His holy word, and what He has declared will most certainly be. Wise and blessed is he who remembers his end, and prepares himself beforehand.

sections.heading: Do no wrong, pray always, call your people brothers

pairs.en: 9) Wise and blessed is he who wrongs no one, either in word or deed, but blesses everyone as far as he is able. He who sows good seed will also reap good fruit.

10) Wise and blessed is he who prays to God at all times, and seeks from Him mercy, help and protection from the enemy — the devil and his servants, evil men. God does not forsake those who trust in Him.

11) Sensible and good is he who, having peasants, servants and those under him, deals with them as with brothers. For we are all brothers: we have one Father, God, to whom we also pray: “Our Father, which art in the heavens,” and the rest. We are all servants: we have one Lord in the heavens, who is no respecter of persons. Christ, our Lord and King of kings, Lord of lords, calls us brothers: *“I will declare Thy name unto My brethren.”* [Hebrews 2:12] How much more, then, ought every man, even one of high estate, to call all those under him brothers, for we are all men — high and low alike — and all have one God, Father and Lord. Yet a master must keep those under him in fear, and restrain the disorderly, so that they do not become corrupted and perish. In this too consists Christian wisdom.

sections.heading: Time, virtue, and the one Redeemer

pairs.en: 12) Time, once lost, does not return, any more than a word once spoken; it should not be spent in idleness, in revelry and other unprofitable pursuits, but in useful and godly labours. *“In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread,”* God says to man. [Genesis 3:19]

13) True Christian wisdom is to overcome one's natural evil disposition — that is, pride, arrogance, anger, malice, envy, hatred, impurity, sensuality, love of money, avarice, intemperance and the rest — and to follow the example of Christ's holy life: His humility, love, mercy, patience, meekness and His other beautiful, divine virtues. To this His holy apostles exhort us, and Christ Himself teaches: *“I am the light of the world: he that followeth Me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life.”* [John 8:12] From this it follows that whoever does not follow the example of Christ's life walks in darkness and goes astray.

14) The God-fearing Christian, who carries out his Christian duty, must place his hope of salvation in nothing else than Jesus Christ alone, the Son of God, the Redeemer of the world, who redeemed us from death and hell, *“not with silver or gold,”* but with His own precious Blood. [1 Peter 1:18–19] *“I am the way, the truth, and the life,”* He says; *“no man cometh unto the Father, but by Me.”* [John 14:6] Glory be to Him for this, with the Father and the Holy Spirit!

In this, then, consists Christian wisdom, which is found not in the doctrines of the wise men of this age, but in the doctrines of the prophets and apostles, who preached to us the Word of God, being enlightened by His Holy Spirit. [1 Peter 1:25] This wisdom consists not in words, but in power. This wisdom is unknown and unwelcome to the world, but beloved of God. Seek, then, this wisdom by reading and pondering the holy Word of God, and by earnest prayer. May God, the Source of wisdom and of every good thing, make us wise unto our salvation and to the glory of His holy name.
